events.title: A Meteor Shard!
events.body: A warm blue stone is humming in the center circle. The groundskeeper insists it was not there yesterday.

choices.label: Put it in the trophy case

outcomes.successHeadline: The queue goes round the block
outcomes.text: The shard becomes a glittering local attraction and fans queue around the block.
It cools into a perfectly ordinary rock. The trophy cabinet looks embarrassed.
A delighted geology department pays promptly and promises not to ask about the scorch mark.

events.title: Mysterious Energy Drink
events.body: A salesman in mirrored glasses offers one unlabelled crate and refuses to blink.

outcomes.successHeadline: The cones got alphabetized
outcomes.text: The squad trains at impossible speed and alphabetizes the cones before cooling down.
It tastes like warm cucumber. Everyone spends the afternoon burping in unison.
The salesman vanishes. One useful cooler remains behind.

events.title: The Abandoned Lab
events.body: A team-building bus takes a wrong turn and stops outside a laboratory marked DEFINITELY EMPTY.

outcomes.successHeadline: The lab pays a grant
outcomes.text: The motion sensors wake up and award the club a research grant for excellent footwork.
The only discovery is a vending machine that accepts coins but gives nothing back.
The driver finds the training camp. Nobody mentions the moving curtains.

events.title: Your Hero Gets a Commercial
events.body: The sponsor wants a hero to advertise cereal by blasting open an indestructible breakfast box.

outcomes.successHeadline: That catchphrase is everywhere
outcomes.text: The box explodes into harmless golden flakes. The catchphrase is on every playground by Monday.
The box survives. The spoon does not. The sponsor still pays the appearance fee.
The hero says 'crunch' with tremendous authority.

events.title: A Player in a Slump
events.body: One player stays behind after training, taking the same tired shot again and again.

outcomes.successHeadline: The cardboard dragon works
outcomes.text: Shooting through a cardboard dragon works. The whole squad demands a turn.
The dragon falls over before the first shot. At least everyone laughs.
A quiet day away from training clears their head.

events.title: Two Players Feud
events.body: Two lockers are now separated by a line of cones and a handwritten border checkpoint.

choices.label: Enter them in a duet challenge

outcomes.successHeadline: The worst anthem ever written
outcomes.text: Their terrible club anthem wins the room and the border checkpoint comes down.
They argue about the chorus. Bert confiscates the microphone.
They cooperate long enough to move a giant tire and forget the original argument.

events.title: A Kid Asks for a Hero
events.body: A handwritten letter asks whether a club hero can visit the local school and rescue sports day.

choices.label: Let the hero run sports day

outcomes.successHeadline: Losing the race on purpose
outcomes.text: The hero loses the egg-and-spoon race on purpose and wins every heart in the playground.
One enthusiastic demonstration launches the beanbag onto the roof. The children call it brilliant.
The class sends back a team photo and thirty-seven tactical suggestions.

events.title: The Scoreboard Predicts Tomorrow
events.body: At midnight the scoreboard displays a result for a match that has not happened yet.

outcomes.successHeadline: The preparation looks like magic
outcomes.text: Every predicted moment arrives. The club's preparation looks like magic.
The display showed tomorrow's maintenance date, not a score. The training session still gives everyone a useful laugh.
It continues glowing for six seconds, then behaves perfectly forever.

events.title: Four Without Losing
events.body: A local TV station wants a two-minute interview about how your small club went four matches without losing.

outcomes.successHeadline: The whole division took notes
outcomes.text: You explain the full plan on TV. The team keeps winning, and more people come to watch.
Three managers copy the plan by Tuesday. Two of them do it better.

choices.label: Thank the players and end the interview

outcomes.text: You name all eighteen players until the interview time runs out.

events.title: Into the Next Cup Round
events.body: You won the cup match, and the scoreboard operator has left the final score up all week on purpose.

choices.label: Leave the score up until the next round

outcomes.successHeadline: Nobody touched the switch for a week
outcomes.text: Supporters detour past the ground just to look at it. The next opponent arrives and reads it twice.
A storm knocks out the second digit. It now reads a much stranger result.

choices.label: Reset it and get back to the league

outcomes.text: The operator photographs it, then resets it, then photographs it again.

events.title: A Thousand Voices
events.body: The turnstile counter passes a thousand and the man who operates it insists on a photograph with it.

choices.label: Open the far side of the ground

outcomes.successHeadline: The far side sings back
outcomes.text: The far terrace fills, learns its own songs by half time, and starts answering the main stand.
Eleven people spread themselves across four hundred seats and enjoy the room.
The photograph goes in the programme. He buys forty copies for relatives.

events.title: A Rival Bids
events.body: A club two divisions higher has offered money for one of your players. You have eight days to decide.

outcomes.successHeadline: The answer travels faster than the bid
outcomes.text: Your flat refusal reaches the dressing room before it reaches their chairman. The rival chairman decides you meant it about all of them.
Their scout keeps turning up anyway, now with a folding chair.
The fee is higher than you expected, and the eight-day deadline is firm. Bert writes down both details.

events.title: Final Transfer Offer
events.body: A rival club has offered $2,600 for one of your players. The offer expires at 5 p.m.

choices.label: Reject the offer and keep them

outcomes.successHeadline: They stay after the 5 p.m. deadline
outcomes.text: The deadline passes. They stay at the club and are pleased that you rejected the offer.
The offer expires, but they are upset that you never discussed it with them.
The rival pays $2,600. They leave for their club that afternoon.

events.title: Two Clubs Want the Same Player
events.body: A player you have scouted all month is meeting a rival club's scout in a cafe.

outcomes.successHeadline: The second coffee was yours
outcomes.text: You offer the same amount, and he signs a quick agreement before the rival scout returns.
He thanks you both, chooses neither, and moves to a club by the sea.
Your scout spends the afternoon on someone cheaper and, he insists, better.

events.title: A Club Legend Walks In
events.body: A man who played four hundred games here in the seventies is standing in reception holding his own boots.

choices.label: Ask him to take a session

outcomes.successHeadline: One drill, forty years old, still works
outcomes.text: He runs one drill he has sworn by since 1974. It is baffling, exhausting, and by Friday the squad asks for it again.
He mostly tells stories. Excellent stories, and a warm afternoon for everyone.

choices.label: Put the boots in the cabinet

outcomes.text: The boots go on the middle shelf. He visits every other Saturday to check on them.

events.title: The Young Player Who Keeps Scoring
events.body: The youth coach says one young player has scored in every training match.

choices.label: Put them in with the first team

outcomes.successHeadline: Their scoring record was real
outcomes.text: They score twice in front of the senior squad. The team stays after training to watch them.
They struggle with the senior team for the full match, but learn more in that hour than in a month.

choices.label: Leave them where they are winning

outcomes.text: The youth coach is delighted, which is rare, and hands over a session plan built around them.

events.title: A Selling Club Needs Cash
events.body: Your scout learns that one club on the Deals list needs cash for urgent roof repairs. Their director wants a transfer done quickly.

choices.label: Let the repair bill reach the press

outcomes.successHeadline: The price drops
outcomes.text: The story brings other creditors to the door. The director calls first and cuts the asking fee by 15%.
The director learns that the leak came from your club and adds 10% to the asking fee.
The director values certainty and cuts the asking fee by 5%.

events.title: The West Stand Leaks
events.body: Four rows of the west stand are now officially a water feature. The safety officer has used the word CLOSED.

choices.label: Patch it with whoever turns up

outcomes.successHeadline: Nine supporters and one long ladder
outcomes.text: Nine supporters, one ladder, and a Sunday. The roof holds, and everyone who helped now owns a small piece of the ground.
The patch survives one shower. A professional is called, and charges for the diagnosis too.
It costs what it costs and is finished by Friday, dry and entirely unremarkable.

events.title: The West Stand Reopens
events.body: The dry rows go back on sale and the supporters who fixed them want the first four seats.

choices.label: Name the rows after the ladder crew

outcomes.successHeadline: Four seats with nine names on them
outcomes.text: Nine names go on a brass strip along four seats. Every one of them brings somebody new the following week.
The engraver misspells two names. Both men decide they prefer the new versions.

choices.label: Just put them back on sale

outcomes.text: They sell out in a morning, mostly to people who now check the roof out of habit.

events.title: Fans Start a Choir
events.body: Six fans in the stands have started singing together and want a microphone.

outcomes.successHeadline: Six voices, then sixty
outcomes.text: Six voices become sixty by half time. The terrace has a sound now, and it is genuinely quite good.
They attempt a key nobody can reach. The attempt itself becomes the joke of the season.

choices.label: Let them sing without a microphone

outcomes.text: They sing anyway, all afternoon, and are hoarse and happy by full time.

events.title: The Fans Add a New Verse
events.body: The fan choir has written a four-minute second verse about the club's plumbing.

outcomes.successHeadline: The boiler song becomes a local hit
outcomes.text: The full song is released and becomes a local hit. The boiler is now famous across the county.
Four minutes proves to be three minutes too many. The chorus survives; the verse does not.
The trimmed chorus is sung on the way out of every home game from then on.

events.title: The Postman Claims To Be Faster
events.body: The postman has told the whole street they are quicker than your quickest player. Your quickest player has heard.

outcomes.successHeadline: The postman is beaten by a street
outcomes.text: Four hundred people watch a professional footballer beat a postman, and cheer anyway.
Your player stops after forty metres with a pulled hamstring, in front of everyone.
They run on an empty pitch with a stopwatch. Their sprint time improves without an audience.

events.title: Hit the Crossbar Ten Times
events.body: A player wants to stay until they have hit the crossbar ten times. It is already dark.

outcomes.successHeadline: The tenth shot hits the underside of the crossbar
outcomes.text: After nine hundred shots, the tenth hits the crossbar and they finally go home.
After six hundred shots, their technique gets worse instead of better.
Ten minutes, four attempts, one clean strike to finish on.

events.title: The Keep-Away Drill Never Ends
events.body: The squad has made a keep-away drill where one player stays in the middle until they win the ball. They have been there since Tuesday.

choices.label: Keep them in the middle all week

outcomes.successHeadline: They learn to read every pass early
outcomes.text: By Friday they are intercepting passes the passer has not decided to make yet.
By Friday they have stopped chasing it at all.
Everybody takes a turn in the middle and the drill works as designed.

events.title: Mark The Hero All Week
events.body: One of your defenders wants to spend the week training against your best attacker: stay tight to them all session, block every ball. The hero thinks it is a great idea.

outcomes.successHeadline: By Thursday the hero asks them to stop
outcomes.text: The hero spends four days going nowhere and asks, on Thursday, whether the defender can mark somebody else.
The hero beats them again and again in front of the squad for four days.
Half an hour is enough to learn something and not enough to be humiliated.

events.title: The Indoor Football League Needs a Player
events.body: The local indoor football league needs one more player. The hall is small, the floor is concrete, and the tackles are hard.

choices.label: Let them join the six-week league

outcomes.successHeadline: Their ball control improves
outcomes.text: Six weeks of indoor football gives them much better control of the ball.
A bad landing on the concrete floor leaves them injured.

choices.label: Let them play one practice game

outcomes.text: One game, no scores kept, and a touch that is noticeably tidier by Thursday.

events.title: They Have Asked, In Writing
events.body: They have asked to train twice a day. In writing. With a schedule attached, and a second schedule for the first schedule.

outcomes.successHeadline: They finish the week fitter than anyone at the club
outcomes.text: Ten sessions in five days, and on Saturday they are still running when everyone else has stopped.
The extra work sends them into the treatment room by Wednesday afternoon.
One session, done properly, and a night's sleep at the end of it.

events.title: Forty Penalties, Right Now
events.body: The squad has decided your keeper should face forty penalties. Your keeper has agreed.

outcomes.successHeadline: They save the last one and lie down on the goal line
outcomes.text: By the thirtieth they have stopped diving early and started reading hips.
By the thirtieth they have stopped reading anything and started guessing.
Ten penalties, three saved, and everyone goes in before it gets silly.

events.title: Their Childhood Club Invites Them Back
events.body: Their childhood club has invited them to play all 90 minutes in a tribute match on Sunday.

choices.label: Let them play the full match

outcomes.successHeadline: They get a standing ovation from four hundred people
outcomes.text: Four hundred people who watched them grow up give them a standing ovation when they leave the field.
After twenty minutes on a badly maintained pitch, they leave the field injured.
The shirt is framed behind the bar by Monday lunchtime.

events.title: They Miss A Specific Bakery
events.body: A young player misses their mother, their dog, and their favourite bakery back home.

choices.label: Move the family near the ground

outcomes.successHeadline: Their mother is at every home game by October
outcomes.text: The club pays the deposit. By October their mother has a seat she considers hers.
They come, they hate it, and they are gone again by the second month. The deposit does not come back.
Two days at home and a box of something from the bakery on the way back.

events.title: They Want Regular Playing Time
events.body: Their agent is discussing a new contract. The player wants regular playing time before they sign.

choices.label: Promise them a regular starting place

outcomes.successHeadline: They sign before the agent finishes their coffee
outcomes.text: You say it plainly and they sign before their agent has finished the coffee.
They repeat the promise to a local reporter, word for word, on the record.

choices.label: Be honest and make no promises

outcomes.text: You tell them what you honestly think, which is more than most managers offer.

events.title: A Full Day With The Cameras
events.body: A local TV show wants to film your most popular player for a full day.

outcomes.successHeadline: The show airs twice and their shirts sell out
outcomes.text: The show airs twice in one weekend, and the shop sells out of shirts with their squad number.
The edit finds every dropped pass and none of the good ones.
Twenty minutes, two good answers, and everyone is home by four.

events.title: One Place Left In The Hills
events.body: A recovery camp up in the hills has one place left this week. It is not cheap and the food is famously terrible.

outcomes.successHeadline: They come back down looking like a different athlete
outcomes.text: Six days of thin air and terrible food, and they come back down transformed.
Altitude, bad sleep, worse food, and legs heavier than when they left.
A quiet week, no travel, and legs that feel like their own again.

events.title: Six Tuesdays For A Certificate
events.body: A coaching course runs Tuesdays for six weeks. Tuesday is a training day. The course does not care.

choices.label: Send them properly, miss the Tuesdays

outcomes.successHeadline: They come back running sessions nobody here has seen
outcomes.text: Six Tuesdays gone and they return with sessions nobody at this level has run before.
Six Tuesdays gone, one laminated certificate, no visible difference.
They do the evenings, keep their Tuesdays, and pick up two useful things.

events.title: Two Weeks at a Bigger Club
events.body: A club two divisions higher will let one of your coaches watch their work for two weeks. They have offered them a bed at their training ground.

outcomes.successHeadline: They come home with new coaching ideas
outcomes.text: They spend fourteen days watching the bigger club train and bring their best ideas home.
They return with a system that needs players with skills this club does not have.

choices.label: Ask for their session notes instead

outcomes.text: They send eleven pages. Four of them are usable here.

events.title: Give Me The Week
events.body: Your assistant has asked for one week running everything. Not a session. The whole week.

outcomes.successHeadline: Their weeks are worth more than they were on Monday
outcomes.text: Five days, their plan, and the squad arrives on Saturday sharper than it left.
By Wednesday it is clear the week had no plan in it at all.
One session, their own plan, and it goes perfectly well.

events.title: They Want The Lights Off
events.body: They want to give the team talk in the dark. They have explained why twice and it has not helped.

outcomes.successHeadline: Nobody says a word for a full minute afterwards
outcomes.text: Eleven grown men sit in the dark and afterwards nobody speaks for a full minute.
Eleven grown men sit in the dark and cannot look at each other for a week.
They speak well. The lights stay on. Everyone is slightly relieved.

events.title: They Used To Keep Goal
events.body: Your keeper works alone. One of your staff kept goal until their knees stopped them, and has said so out loud.

outcomes.successHeadline: They are a goalkeeping coach now, and the gloves came back out
outcomes.text: Three weeks of courses and the gloves come back out of the loft for good.
It turns out they remember a great deal less than they told everybody.
An hour on Thursdays, which is an hour more than the keeper had.

events.title: Two Coaches, Two Drills
events.body: The head coach and assistant have designed different versions of the same drill. Choose which coach to support.

outcomes.successHeadline: The chosen drill works
outcomes.text: You support one coach in front of the other. Their drill works, and the argument ends by Friday.
Their drill does not work, and the whole squad sees it fail all week.

choices.label: Use each drill for half the week

outcomes.text: Half a week each, no argument settled, no harm done.

events.title: A Fire Destroys Twelve Years of Notes
events.body: A boiler fire destroyed twelve years of training notes on Sunday night. The coach is trying to stay calm.

choices.label: Rewrite all the notes from memory

outcomes.successHeadline: The new notes are better than the old ones
outcomes.text: A month of evenings, and the new folder is sharper than the one that burned.
Half of what they write from memory turns out to be wrong.

choices.label: Print the four years the club saved

outcomes.text: The club had four seasons backed up. They take what they can get.

events.title: A Salesman With a Tracking System
events.body: A salesperson says their laptop can track eleven player statistics. They claim all eleven will improve training.

outcomes.successHeadline: One measurement improves training
outcomes.text: Ten measurements are useless. The eleventh helps the coaches plan a better training week.
None of the eleven measurements help. The salesman keeps the deposit.
Two weeks free, one useful chart, no invoice.

events.title: The Groundskeeper Has His Own Mix
events.body: The groundskeeper has developed his own grass seed mix and won a small local award for it.

outcomes.successHeadline: By September it is the best surface in the division
outcomes.text: By September visiting managers are asking what is in it. He will not say.
The grass grows in bare patches by October, and the damage spreads.

choices.label: Buy the mix the league recommends

outcomes.text: The league's mix goes down. It is fine. It is extremely fine.

events.title: Forty Fans Offer to Help
events.body: Forty fans have offered to work for one weekend. They are enthusiastic, but none are qualified builders.

choices.label: Let the fans do the work

outcomes.successHeadline: They finish the work on Sunday night
outcomes.text: Forty people, two days, and on Sunday night nobody wants to go home.
The fans mean well, but much of their work must be done again.

choices.label: Take the materials and hire professionals

outcomes.text: The fans buy the materials, professional builders do the work, and everyone is happy.

events.title: Training Equipment From a Promoted Club
events.body: A club promoted to a higher division has sent a crate of used training equipment. Nobody here knows what half of it does.

outcomes.successHeadline: The unknown machine becomes a team favourite
outcomes.text: The machine nobody could name turns out to be the one everybody queues for.
Two machines nobody can use permanently block part of the training room.

choices.label: Keep only the equipment you understand

outcomes.text: The useful equipment is installed. The rest goes into storage.

events.title: The Physio Has a Sleep Plan
events.body: The physio wants the players to sleep better in the dorm: blackout blinds, fixed bedtimes, and no screens after 10 p.m.

outcomes.successHeadline: The squad wakes up rested on Saturday
outcomes.text: The blinds, fixed bedtime, and screen ban help the whole squad sleep better.
The players sleep badly for two weeks and blame the new routine.
The blackout blinds are installed. After two weeks, everyone notices that they sleep better.

events.title: An Evening Friendly Match
events.body: The club can host an evening friendly match, keep the shop open late, and invite the fan choir. The floodlights are old.

outcomes.successHeadline: Nine hundred fans stay after the match
outcomes.text: The lights hold, the choir sings, and nine hundred people stay behind afterwards.
Half the floodlights fail when the match starts, and the rest are too dim.

choices.label: Open the shop an hour early instead

outcomes.text: An extra hour, a decent queue, no risk taken.

events.title: The New Drill Starts an Argument
events.body: The coach is teaching a new drill for winning the ball back. The squad is still arguing about it an hour later.

choices.label: Build training around the new drill

outcomes.successHeadline: The squad adopts the new style
outcomes.text: Two weeks later, the squad uses the new style without arguing about it.
The new drill falls apart in the next Tuesday training session.
Half of it stays, half of it quietly disappears, nobody mentions it.

events.title: Their Childhood Club Offers to Help
events.body: Their childhood club knows they were injured in the tribute match. The chairman has called twice to offer help.

choices.label: Let them pay for the specialist

outcomes.successHeadline: They return two weeks early and the old club pays the bill
outcomes.text: The old club pays for the specialist, refuses repayment, and the player returns two weeks early.
A second doctor and a third scan delay their recovery longer than either club expected.
Their physio drives over twice a week and will not take a fee.

events.title: Forty Fans Want Their Names on the Wall
events.body: The forty fans who helped with the building want all their names on the wall. They have brought an alphabetical list.

outcomes.successHeadline: Forty names in brass, and forty families who come to see them
outcomes.text: Forty names in brass, and forty families who turn up on the Saturday to find them.
Three names are misspelled. In brass. Permanently.

choices.label: Use one plaque with one thank-you line

outcomes.text: A well-made plaque thanking all forty fans is fixed beside the door.

events.title: They Want the Promise in Their Contract
events.body: You promised them regular starts, and they have started every match since. They want that promise added to their contract now.

choices.label: Add the starting promise to their contract

outcomes.successHeadline: They sign for one extra year
outcomes.text: The promise goes into their contract, and they sign for one year longer than their agent advised.
They read the contract and find it guarantees fewer starts than you promised.
You say it again, out loud, and they take you at your word again.

events.title: Their Agent Saved Your Promise
events.body: You promised them regular starts, but they have not played. Their agent saved the newspaper quote.

choices.label: Start them in Saturday's match anyway

outcomes.successHeadline: They prove they should have been playing
outcomes.text: They play well and prove they deserved more starts.
They are not ready, and a full match makes that clear to everyone.

choices.label: Admit you broke the promise and apologise

outcomes.text: You clearly admit you were wrong, and the apology helps.

events.title: A Three-Goal Match
events.body: They scored three goals and took the match ball home. They have not put it down since.

choices.label: Nominate them for Player of the Month

outcomes.successHeadline: They read their name out at the ground
outcomes.text: They win it, and the announcer reads their name out at the ground before kickoff.
They read every article about themself and lose focus in training.

choices.label: Frame it for the clubhouse wall

outcomes.text: The ball goes on the wall above the bar, signed by everybody who was there.

events.title: Groundskeeper Mugs Sell Out
events.body: The club shop has sold all 400 mugs printed with the groundskeeper on them.

outcomes.successHeadline: The groundskeeper starts signing them
outcomes.text: The 4,000 new mugs sell out in two weeks, and the groundskeeper starts signing them at the gate.
Four thousand mugs sit unsold. The groundskeeper stops coming into the shop.
The next 400 mugs also sell out in two weeks.
